Class DeploymentWizard.Builder

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.design.optimizer.wizard.DeploymentWizard.Builder
Enclosing class:
DeploymentWizard
public static final class DeploymentWizard.Builder extends Object
Fluent builder for configuring a deployment plan. Provides methods to set Cloud Router package, connection types, backbone topology, bandwidth strategy, routing protocol settings, and account details.

  • Method Details

    • routerPackage

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder routerPackage(String packageCode)
      Sets the Cloud Router package code from its string form, leniently: the value is trimmed and upper-cased before being resolved (so "standard" and " Premium " both work). Defaults to GatewayPackageCode.STANDARD.

      The code is validated here — once, at plan time — so a bad value fails fast instead of surfacing as an IllegalArgumentException mid-deployment in DeploymentPlan.execute() after some routers have already been provisioned.

      Parameters:
      packageCode - the router package code (case-insensitive)
      Returns:
      this builder for method chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the code does not name a deployable package tier

    • routerNamePrefix

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder routerNamePrefix(String prefix)
      Sets the naming prefix for Cloud Routers and the connection / routing-protocol names derived from them. Each router is named "{prefix}-{metroCode}" (e.g. "FCR-DC") and a provider connection "{prefix}-{metroCode}-to-{token}" (e.g. "FCR-DC-to-aws"). Defaults to "FCR".

      The prefix is the stem of every generated name, and Fabric rejects any name of 24 or more characters. The prefix is therefore trimmed, reduced to name-safe characters, and bounded to a short budget at plan time: a prefix longer than that budget is truncated (the composed names always stay within the limit), and a blank prefix is rejected with an IllegalArgumentException when plan() runs, because there is no stem to build on.

      Parameters:
      prefix - the router name prefix
      Returns:
      this builder for method chaining

    • providerConnectionType

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder providerConnectionType(ConnectionType type)
      Sets the Fabric connection type for provider connections. Defaults to IP_VC — the only type Fabric accepts for a connection whose A-side is a Cloud Router, which every wizard-planned provider connection has. Setting a type incompatible with an FCR A-side (e.g. the port-based EVPL_VC) is flagged by the plan's Layer-1 validation (FCR A-side => IP_VC) rather than 400ing live.
      Parameters:
      type - the connection type for provider connections
      Returns:
      this builder for method chaining

    • backboneConnectionType

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder backboneConnectionType(ConnectionType type)
      Sets the Fabric connection type for backbone links. Defaults to IP_VC — a backbone link is Cloud Router to Cloud Router, and Fabric accepts an FCR-originated virtual connection only as IP_VC. An incompatible type is flagged by the plan's Layer-1 validation (FCR A-side => IP_VC).
      Parameters:
      type - the connection type for backbone links
      Returns:
      this builder for method chaining

    • customBandwidthMap

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder customBandwidthMap(Map<String,Integer> bandwidthMap)
      Sets a custom bandwidth map for BandwidthStrategy.CUSTOM. Values are bandwidth in Mbps; keys are matched per (metro, provider) most-specific-first as either "<metroId>-<providerLabel>" (a per-metro-per-provider override, e.g. "DC-Amazon Web Services") or "<providerLabel>" (that provider in every metro, e.g. "Amazon Web Services"). A (metro, provider) connection with no matching key is sized by the normal per-workload aggregation instead of a fabricated default.
      Parameters:
      bandwidthMap - the custom bandwidth mapping
      Returns:
      this builder for method chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the map is null or any of its values is null — a null bandwidth cannot size a connection, so it fails fast here naming the offending key instead of surfacing as an NPE mid-plan

    • subnetBase

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder subnetBase(String subnetBase)
      Sets the base network the plan's /30 peering subnets are allocated from. Defaults to "10.100.0.0": the first connection peers on 10.100.0.1/30 / 10.100.0.2/30, and each further connection advances the third octet.

      Cross-plan reuse caveat: allocation is scoped to a single plan, so every plan restarts from this base. Plans executed into the same project would therefore reuse the same peering addresses — give each such plan a distinct base (e.g. .subnetBase("10.200.0.0")) to keep their /30s disjoint.

      Parameters:
      subnetBase - an IPv4 dotted-quad base network, e.g. "10.200.0.0" (the fourth octet is ignored; allocation advances the third)
      Returns:
      this builder for method chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the value is not a valid IPv4 dotted-quad

    • notifications

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder notifications(String... emails)
      Adds notification email addresses for provisioning updates. Every address is applied to every planned Cloud Router and connection (Fabric mandates at least one recipient per Cloud Router, error EQ-3040013) — all of them are sent on the wire bodies and rendered into exported HCL, never just the first.

      Repeated calls accumulate — addresses from every call are kept, none replaced. A plan built with no recipient at all fails Layer-1 validation.

      Parameters:
      emails - one or more email addresses
      Returns:
      this builder for method chaining
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an address is null or blank
      NullPointerException - if the array itself is null

    • rateCard

      public DeploymentWizard.Builder rateCard(RateCard rateCard)
      Sets the rate card used to price the plan. When omitted, the wizard defaults to live Equinix pricing (EquinixRateCard.of(fabric)), falling back to a built-in heuristic for any resource the live catalogue cannot price.

      Supply a CustomRateCard (or a layered card) to price against your own negotiated rates instead.

      Parameters:

    • reprice

      public DeploymentPlan reprice(DeploymentPlan plan)
      Reprices a plan whose connections changed (e.g. an MCP profile choice altered a billable tier) and returns the result as a new DeploymentPlan: the argument is never mutated (plans are immutable values), so callers must use the returned copy — whose monthly and setup totals match the plan's current connections rather than the tiers they were originally priced at.

      The plan's current Cloud Routers, provider connections and backbone links are re-priced against this builder's rate card and commitment term — the same configuration the plan was built with — through the wizard's single pricing authority (DeploymentWizardEngine.estimatePricing), so per-metro currency reconciliation is preserved exactly as at plan time. Only the plan's pricing is replaced; every other field is carried through unchanged. Repricing a plan whose connections did not change yields the same figures (a no-op-equivalent).

      Parameters:
      plan - the plan whose pricing is stale relative to its current connections; left untouched by this call
      Returns:
      a new copy of the plan with pricing recomputed from its current connections
